entry.title: Day 16: The Human Connection in Code
entry.summary: Today I designed a mental health website. Coincidentally, I also felt like a human for the first time in forever - turns out my friend calling had something to do with that. Last night: Went to sleep after critiquing every single idea I'd come up with Tonight: Will probably fall asleep doing ridge regression examples I'm behind my schedule, but it's probably worth it. (That's what I keep telling myself.) There's something weird about coding in isolation. You get so deep into the problem-solving zone that you forget the outside world exists. Then someone calls, and suddenly you remember you're not just a debugging machine. The mental health website design felt different today - maybe because I was actually connecting with the human side of what I was building. Still juggling ML daily tasks while expanding into other areas. Sometimes you just have to see what clicks. Connect on discord for daily updates and fellow future entrepreneurs.

entry.title: 👨‍💻 What is Request Coalescing?
entry.summary: Recently, I encountered a scenario where multiple API requests were being made from a common function triggered by various initiators. To address this, I discovered the concept of request coalescing. Request coalescing is a technique for tracking ongoing API requests and sharing the result among all simultaneous requests. In applications that rely on authentication tokens, it's common for multiple parts of the app to trigger requests around the same time. If the token has expired, these requests might all attempt a token refresh simultaneously. Request coalescing ensures that only one refresh request is actually made. All subsequent requests receive the result of that shared ongoing promise, avoiding redundant network calls and improving performance. Check out the code snippet below :- let…
